title: I Reported the Silent Second Set of Books at the Bakery

parts.text: I counted the till twice and the envelope still did not match. I am twenty-four, closer, flour in my hair. The manager, Rhea, kept a second notebook under the mixer. It smelled like vanilla extract and dust. My coworker Tomas had warned me not to touch the black book. Tips were supposed to split. The book said HOUSE. I photographed two pages, dates, amounts. The mixer had a hairline crack I always stared at when nervous. Rhea said, "That's not for staff" I said, "The tips are" Rhea came back for her jacket. The street outside was wet, orange from the bakery sign. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She knows I saw the HOUSE column, and the photo is still in my camera roll.

parts.text: I emailed the owner, Mr. Delaney, from the bus with flour still on my sleeves. He is old-school and hates surprises more than theft. He came at 6 a.m. and asked Rhea to open the mixer cabinet. The book was there. Tomas confirmed the HOUSE weeks. Rhea called it a rainy-day fund. Delaney called it wages. We got a real tip pool and a cheap lockbox. Rhea moved to mornings at a different shop he also owns. I still close. The mixer crack is still there. I fill it with a glance instead of a notebook. Delaney said, "Why does this say HOUSE" Rhea said, "It's a buffer" Tomas bought everyone day-old croissants. They were a little stale. We ate them anyway. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i.
